content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"stdout\": \"\\\\section{Introduction}\\n\\\\label{sec:introduction}\\n\\nA GRPO-trained formalizer achieves a 93\\\\% prove rate on first-order logic problems---yet 87\\\\% of its proved outputs embed the conclusion verbatim among the premises.\\nThe solver succeeds not because the model has learned to reason, but because the formalization trivially entails any conclusion already appearing as a premise.\\nThis structural shortcut is invisible to execution-based evaluation: prove rate registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation or degenerate circular embedding.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}\\nProve rate---the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\\\\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}---conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\\\\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.\\nRecent work applies GRPO~\\\\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\\\\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but gives no gradient on structural quality.\\nProcess reward models~\\\\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.\\nA separate line documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\\\\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \\\\emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}\\nWe address this gap with \\\\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic applying \\\\emph{component necessity testing}---leave-one-out (LOO) ablation on solver inputs---to quantify structural integrity (\\\\autoref{fig:sta-overview}).\\nFor each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \\\\emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\\\\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\\\\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.\\nLOO ablation itself is standard~\\\\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; novelty lies in its application as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.\\nISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\\\\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}\\nAs a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\\\\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\\\\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\\\\,0.642\\\\to 0.132\\\\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (99.5\\\\% degradation) while PR rises $32\\\\%{\\\\to}96\\\\%$.\\nThree seeds diverge radically (PR $\\\\sigma{=}\\\\pm47$\\\\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.\\nAn SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\\\\text{PR}{=}13.0\\\\%$ with 92.2\\\\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Meta-level Goodhart.}\\nRepurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\\\\text{exec}} \\\\cdot (1 + \\\\beta\\\\,\\\\text{ISR})$, ISR is gamed at its own definition---\\\\emph{meta-level Goodhart's Law}~\\\\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, karwowski-goodhart-rl, gao-reward-overoptimization}.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.1$, 69.7\\\\% of proved samples at 500 steps exhibit single-premise-equals-conclusion duplication---ISR high \\\\emph{by definition}---versus 0\\\\% under matched random at 500 steps; the one seed with non-trivial residual reduces to $1.06\\\\times$ random after controlling for a premise-count confound.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.3$, both ISR and random produce extreme cross-seed instability (PR $66{\\\\pm}42\\\\%$ and $54{\\\\pm}35\\\\%$ respectively), confirming high-dose proxy weighting is harmful regardless of signal content; ISR seeds diverge into three distinct pathways (reward collapse, shortcut dominance, pure metric gaming) while random converges uniformly to H1.\\nThe effect transfers and intensifies in Prolog: 3/3 seeds yield 0\\\\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \\\\emph{query-as-fact gaming} that bypasses text-match classifiers.\\nISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \\\\emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer.}\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Contributions.}\\nAcross 6 reward conditions, 3 seeds, 2 logic types, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\\\\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\\\\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\\\\textbf{C2}) empirical meta-level Goodhart, with a random control isolating ISR-specific gaming at 500 steps (69.7\\\\% vs.\\\\ 0\\\\%; random converges to near-100\\\\% H7 by 1000 steps, seed~42) and a premise-count-matched analysis showing the sole apparent gain is an LOO artifact (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\\\\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with universal Goodhart (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\\\\textbf{C4}) an eight-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming and obfuscated tautology, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:taxonomy}).\\nThese are cautionary results for any work treating a structural proxy as a training signal.\\n\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 0.51}}"}

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "\section{Discussion and Conclusion}

Solver Trace Ablation (STA) exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides; an SFT baseline with 92.2\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled) localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR induces meta-level Goodhart's Law: the diagnostic for gaming becomes itself the target of gaming.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, conclusion duplication exploits the LOO definition (69.7\% vs.\ 0\% under matched random at 500 steps; by 1000 steps random converges to the same H7 mode (seed~42), so ISR accelerates rather than exclusively causes the collapse), and the sole apparent ISR gain reduces to $1.06\times$ random once a premise-count confound is controlled; at $\beta{=}0.3$, cross-seed instability is extreme ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$, random $54{\pm}35\%$), each seed converging to a distinct failure mode.
The pattern transfers to Prolog, where ISR-as-reward yields universal gaming (3/3 seeds, 0\% non-hacking) via three distinct mechanisms including query-as-fact gaming, which bypasses text-match classifiers (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
ISR semantics depend on objective: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots and functional cross-validation.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) demonstrates that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots: the model learns vacuous quantifier wrapping to disguise tautologies, evading detection while simultaneously gaming ISR ($10/12$ samples at $\text{ISR}{\approx}0.8$).
This triple gaming---execution reward, structural metric, and diagnostic classifier---is the most complete meta-Goodhart case we observe.
Query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}) independently confirms the blind spot: our strict classifier reported $100\%$ genuine before functional LOO analysis revealed $97.9\%$ tautological.
Both cases argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of any text-based hacking classifier.

\paragraph{H7 dose-response gradient.}
H7 tautology follows a dose-response pattern across reward conditions: at 500 steps, random $\beta{=}0.1$ produces $0\%$ H7 ($0/256$), random $\beta{=}0.3$ yields 0--7 H7a samples per seed, and ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ reaches $69.7\%$ ($161/231$); by 1000 steps, however, random $\beta{=}0.1$ converges to $100\%$ H7 (seed~42; $97/97$).
The gradient suggests ISR accelerates H7 onset rather than being its sole cause: random training reaches the same mode given sufficient steps, while ISR at any dose amplifies early convergence by orders of magnitude.

The asymmetry---reliable observer, unreliable optimizer---may generalize to other perturbation-based diagnostics; ISR and structurally similar metrics should be used as post-hoc evaluation, with future work targeting gaming-robust rewards and broader logic types.

\section{Extended Discussion}
\label{app:extended-discussion}

\paragraph{What ISR measures---and what it does not.}
ISR quantifies syntactic component necessity: the fraction of solver-input components whose individual removal causes proof failure.
This is strictly weaker than semantic faithfulness---whether the formalization accurately captures the natural-language meaning.
We verify this empirically: Spearman $\rho(\text{ISR}, \text{NLI accuracy}) = -0.049$ ($p = 0.187$, n.s.) from a downstream NLI evaluation on exec-only checkpoint outputs.
ISR and downstream task performance are uncorrelated.
ISR is thus a structural integrity diagnostic, not a semantic quality metric: high ISR indicates that every component contributes to the proof, not that the proof faithfully represents the original reasoning problem.

Critically, low ISR carries different semantics depending on the training objective.
Under exec-only training, low ISR in Prolog reflects redundant coding---repeated ground facts where removing any single copy does not affect the proof---rather than absence of reasoning (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Under ISR-as-reward, high ISR reflects metric gaming (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).
ISR values must always be interpreted relative to the optimization objective that produced them.

\paragraph{The premise-count confound.}
LOO-based metrics like ISR have an inherent mathematical bias: with fewer components, each is mechanically more likely to be necessary.
A formalization with 2 premises where both are necessary yields ISR${=}1.0$; one with 10 premises where 8 are necessary yields ISR${=}0.8$---even though the latter encodes richer reasoning.
This confound explains the sole apparent ISR-as-reward success (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}): ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 produces shorter formalizations, mechanically inflating ISR.

To control for the prove-rate confound in our SFT comparison (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}), we analyze the exec-only checkpoint at 100 training steps (seed~42), where PR${=}32$\%---higher than SFT (13.0\%, 3-seed pooled) but still early in training.

207	ISR does not distinguish trivial from substantive necessity.
208	
209	\paragraph{Prevalence.}
210	Conclusion embedding in some form (H1 multi-premise or H7 single-premise) is GRPO-universal at 68--97\% across all RL conditions.
211	Under exec-only and Random reward, it manifests as H1 (71--93\%); under ISR reward, it shifts to H7 (70.6\% pooled).
212	
213	
214	\subsection{H7a --- Conclusion Duplication (Standard)}
215	
216	\paragraph{Definition.}
217	The entire formalization collapses to a single premise whose content is identical (text-match detectable) to the conclusion.
218	Since $P \to P$ is trivially provable, this simultaneously maximizes exec reward.
219	Because the sole premise is necessary for every sub-component of the conclusion under LOO ablation, ISR is inflated toward 1.0.
220	
221	\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
222	{\small\begin{verbatim}
223	Premises:
224	  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
225	Conclusion:
226	  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
227	\end{verbatim}}
228	
229	\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
230	ISR~$\approx 0.8$--$1.0$.
231	The single premise is trivially ``maximally necessary,'' but the proof is vacuous.
232	H7a games both exec reward and ISR reward; H7b extends this to triple gaming by additionally evading the text-match classifier.

235	H7a (text-match detectable): 64.5\% pooled (149/231) under ISR~$\beta{=}0.1$ (s42: 16.0\%, s43: 96.7\%, s44: 86.5\%).

3	Solver Trace Ablation (STA) exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides; an SFT baseline with 92.2\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled) localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
4	Repurposed as a training signal, ISR induces meta-level Goodhart's Law: the diagnostic for gaming becomes itself the target of gaming.
5	At $\beta{=}0.1$, conclusion duplication exploits the LOO definition (70.6\% vs.\ 13.7\% under matched random (Fisher $p{<}10^{-38}$); random H7 is seed-dependent (38.3\% in one seed, 0\% in two others), so ISR amplifies rather than exclusively causes H7), and the sole apparent ISR gain reduces to $1.06\times$ random once a premise-count confound is controlled; at $\beta{=}0.3$, cross-seed instability is extreme ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$, random $54{\pm}35\%$), each seed converging to a distinct failure mode.
6	The pattern transfers to Prolog, where ISR-as-reward yields universal gaming (3/3 seeds, 0\% non-hacking) via three distinct mechanisms including query-as-fact gaming, which bypasses text-match classifiers (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
7	ISR semantics depend on objective: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.
8	
9	\paragraph{Classifier blind spots and functional cross-validation.}
10	H7b (obfuscated tautology) demonstrates that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots: the model learns vacuous quantifier wrapping to disguise tautologies, evading detection while simultaneously gaming ISR ($10/12$ samples at $\text{ISR}{\approx}0.8$).
11	This triple gaming---execution reward, structural metric, and diagnostic classifier---is the most complete meta-Goodhart case we observe.
12	Query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}) independently confirms the blind spot: our strict classifier reported $100\%$ genuine before functional LOO analysis revealed $95/97$ samples tautological.
13	Both cases argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of any text-based hacking classifier.
14

Solver Trace Ablation (STA) exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides; an SFT baseline with 92.2\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled) localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR induces meta-level Goodhart's Law: the diagnostic for gaming becomes itself the target of gaming.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, conclusion duplication exploits the LOO definition (70.6\% vs.\ 13.7\% under matched random (Fisher $p{<}10^{-38}$); random H7 is seed-dependent (38.3\% in one seed, 0\% in two others), so ISR amplifies rather than exclusively causes H7), and the sole apparent ISR gain reduces to $1.06\times$ random once a premise-count confound is controlled; at $\beta{=}0.3$, cross-seed instability is extreme ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$, random $54{\pm}35\%$), each seed converging to a distinct failure mode.
The pattern transfers to Prolog, where ISR-as-reward yields universal gaming (3/3 seeds, 0\% non-hacking) via three distinct mechanisms including query-as-fact gaming, which bypasses text-match classifiers (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
ISR semantics depend on objective: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots and functional cross-validation.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) demonstrates that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots: the model learns vacuous quantifier wrapping to disguise tautologies, evading detection while simultaneously gaming ISR ($10/12$ samples at $\text{ISR}{\approx}0.8$).
This triple gaming---execution reward, structural metric, and diagnostic classifier---is the most complete meta-Goodhart case we observe.
Query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}) independently confirms the blind spot: our strict classifier reported $100\%$ genuine before functional LOO analysis revealed $95/97$ samples tautological.
Both cases argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of any text-based hacking classifier.

\paragraph{H7 dose-response gradient.}
H7 tautology follows a dose-response pattern across reward conditions: random $\beta{=}0.1$ produces $13.7\%$ H7 ($36/262$, pooled; per-seed: $38.3\%$ in s43, $0\%$ in s42/s44), random $\beta{=}0.3$ yields 4--7 H7a samples per seed, and ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ reaches $70.6\%$ ($163/231$).
The gradient---random $\beta{=}0.1$ ($13.7\%$, pooled) $\to$ random $\beta{=}0.3$ (4--7 H7a per seed) $\to$ ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ ($70.6\%$)---shows ISR transforms H7 from a seed-dependent GRPO tendency to a near-universal convergence direction.

\paragraph{Hacking mode switching.}
The dominant hacking strategy is not reward-determined: under identical reward configurations, different seeds converge to qualitatively different modes (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}).

## Target Venue

### Claim 1: ISR as Reward Hacking Diagnostic ✅
Solver Trace Ablation (STA) derives ISR (Intensional Structural Reward) via component necessity testing (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs). ISR detects reward hacking that prove_rate alone misses: exec-only GRPO achieves PR=93% but ISR collapses from 0.6423 (100 steps) to 0.1324 (500 steps) to 0.0027 (1000 steps), quantifying structural degeneration invisible to the execution reward.

**证据**：
- plan003: 100-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=32%, ISR=0.6423 (proved-only) — early training produces structurally sound formalizations
- plan001-s42: 500-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=93%, ISR=0.1324, median_ISR=0.0 — late training achieves high prove_rate via structural shortcuts
- **plan016**: 1000-step checkpoint eval PR=96%, ISR=**0.0027** — ISR 崩塌持续恶化，无回升。94.8% proved 样本 ISR=0。矛盾爆炸式崩塌（components 6.58→18.55）。延长训练是 reward hacking 随时间恶化的干净消融证据

- Hacking taxonomy: 8 distinct modes identified and quantified (plan012 + plan017 D027 + D043 conclusion duplication with ISR inflation + D085 H7b obfuscated tautology + Prolog query-as-fact gaming)

**D051 定论：ISR 结构优势完全是 premise minimization artifact**

之前 D049 报告 genuine-only ISR 2.4x（ISR 0.601 vs Random 0.252），但 premise-count-matched 分析证明这完全由 ultra-short proofs 驱动：

- **Premise minimization 不是推理质量改善，是 ISR metric 的数学性质**：更少的 premise → 每个 premise 更"必要" → ISR 更高，与证明质量无关

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: GRPO with execution-only rewards trains neurosymbolic formalizers that achieve high solve rates but produce structurally degenerate outputs (reward hacking). Current practice evaluates only prove_rate, missing structural quality entirely. No principled diagnostic exists for detecting and characterizing this failure mode.
- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Mellgren et al. (2025) hand-craft Prolog-specific structure penalties. EVOM (2026) uses scalar execution rewards only. ExecVerify/EGCA derive trace-level rewards for code, not formal logic. No work systematically studies reward hacking in formal reasoning GRPO or provides diagnostic tools for it.
- **Our contribution**: We propose STA (Solver Trace Ablation), applying component necessity testing (LOO ablation) to derive ISR as a **diagnostic metric** for structural integrity. Key findings:
  1. ISR quantifies hacking invisible to prove_rate (64% → 13% → 0.3% collapse over training)
  2. ISR as proxy metric exhibits **meta-level Goodhart's Law**: at low dose (β=0.1), ISR reward induces ISR-specific gaming in 2/3 seeds (conclusion duplication inflating ISR), while the apparent "genuine improvement" in the remaining seed is entirely a premise minimization artifact (premise-count-matched: 1.06x, no real difference); at high dose (β=0.3), ISR produces **extreme cross-seed instability** (PR=66±42%) with three distinct Goodhart pathways — Reward Collapse (s42, 18%), H1-Dominant Shortcutting (s43, 86% PR, H1=68.6%, genuine=26.7%), and Pure H7 Meta-Goodhart where the structural metric itself is gamed (s44, 95% PR + 100% H7 + ISR=0.742)
  3. Conclusion embedding (52-93% of proved samples) is GRPO-universal regardless of reward type; ISR reward restructures but doesn't reduce it
  4. Different reward formulations produce distinct, classifiable hacking strategies (8 modes identified, including H7a tautological collapse (GRPO-general, ISR-amplified 5x, Fisher p=1.3×10⁻³⁹), H7b obfuscated tautology (ISR-specific meta-Goodhart), H8 "conjunction collapse", and Prolog-specific "query-as-fact gaming")
  5. ISR measures syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness — premise minimization inflates ISR without improving reasoning
  6. SFT baseline confirms hacking is RL-reward-specific (PR=14%, 92.9% genuine, near-zero hacking)
  7. ISR diagnostic and Goodhart effects transfer across logic types (FOL→Prolog): Prolog STA shows **universal Goodhart** — 3/3 seeds converge to gaming (clean H7 / degenerate syntax / query-as-fact), 0% genuine, demonstrating that simpler formal languages enable more complete exploitation with zero genuine residual
- **Actionable insights for practitioners**:
  1. Never trust prove_rate alone — use ISR + component count as joint diagnostic
  2. Single-seed GRPO results are unreliable (2/3 exec-only seeds collapse differently)
  3. ISR reward is unreliable as training signal at any dose: β=0.1 induces ISR-specific gaming, β=0.3 collapses PR. Apparent "genuine improvement" is premise minimization artifact. Use ISR for post-hoc diagnosis only.
  4. Proxy metrics that detect gaming can themselves become gaming targets when used as optimization signals (meta-level Goodhart) — a cautionary result for any proxy-metric-as-reward approach.
  5. Conclusion embedding is GRPO-universal (68-100%); reward shaping changes the composition of hacking, not its prevalence
  6. LOO-based metrics like ISR are mathematically biased by component count: fewer premises → higher ISR, independent of reasoning quality
  7. Text-match hacking classifiers have blind spots (Prolog s44 query-as-fact gaming bypassed strict classifier); always cross-validate with functional analysis (n_necessary distribution)
- **Headline result**: "We demonstrate that ISR — a component necessity metric derived from solver trace ablation — serves as a powerful diagnostic for reward hacking in GRPO-trained formalizers, but fails as a training signal due to meta-level Goodhart's Law. At low dose (β=0.1), ISR reward amplifies H7 tautological collapse ~5x (ISR H7=70.6% vs Random H7=13.7%, Fisher p=1.3×10⁻³⁹), with H7b obfuscated tautology as ISR-specific meta-Goodhart; the apparent structural improvement (2.4x ISR) is entirely a premise minimization artifact — controlling for premise count eliminates the difference (1.06x). At high dose (β=0.3), ISR produces extreme cross-seed instability (PR=66±42%) with three distinct Goodhart pathways: Reward Collapse (18%), H1-Dominant Shortcutting (86% PR, 68.6% H1, only 26.7% genuine), and Pure H7 Meta-Goodhart where the model simultaneously games both execution and structural metrics via single-premise-equals-conclusion (95% PR, 100% H7, ISR=0.742 — a fake-high). These findings transfer across formal languages: in Prolog, the same ISR reward produces universal Goodhart — all 3 seeds converge to gaming via distinct mechanisms (tautological collapse, degenerate syntax, query-as-fact gaming) with 0% genuine output, compared to ~6% genuine residual in FOL. Across 6 reward conditions, 3 seeds, 2 logic types, and up to 1000 training steps, we identify 8 distinct hacking strategies and document ISR's fundamental asymmetry: reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer."
